title: Where distros differ
summary: Init systems, filesystems, admin groups, firewalls and mandatory access control.

steps.title: Init: systemd and OpenRC
body: Almost every mainstream distro uses **systemd** (module 4). The notable exception is **Alpine**, which uses **OpenRC** (also Gentoo, Artix), and minimal containers often run no init at all.
| start / stop / restart | `systemctl start nginx` | `rc-service nginx start` |
| start at boot | `systemctl enable nginx` | `rc-update add nginx default` |
| don't start at boot | `systemctl disable nginx` | `rc-update del nginx default` |

steps.prompt: Match the systemd command to its OpenRC twin.

steps.title: Filesystems, admin groups, firewalls, MAC
body: **Default filesystems**: Debian/Ubuntu **ext4**; RHEL/Rocky/Alma **xfs** (cannot shrink); Fedora Workstation and openSUSE **btrfs** (snapshots, compression, subvolumes; openSUSE rolls back bad updates with snapper).
**Admin group**: members may use sudo. Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo` group (`usermod -aG sudo ana`). RHEL/Fedora/Arch/SUSE: `wheel` (`usermod -aG wheel ana`). Check `/etc/sudoers` for `%sudo` or `%wheel`.

**Firewall front-ends** (both drive nftables underneath): Ubuntu **ufw** (`ufw allow 443/tcp`, `ufw enable`); RHEL/Fedora/SUSE **firewalld** with zones (`firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=https`, then `--reload`).

**Mandatory access control** (rules that even root processes must obey): RHEL/Fedora **SELinux** labels every file and process (`ls -Z`, `getenforce`, `restorecon`, `setsebool`); Ubuntu/Debian/SUSE **AppArmor** uses per-program path profiles (`aa-status`, profiles in `/etc/apparmor.d`). When a service "has permission" but still gets `Permission denied` on RHEL, check `ausearch -m avc` before anything else, and never "fix" it with `setenforce 0`.

steps.prompt: On Rocky Linux, nginx gets `Permission denied` reading `/srv/site/index.html`, even though the file is `644` and the directories are `755`. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: SELinux: the files lack the `httpd_sys_content_t` label; fix it with `semanage fcontext` + `restorecon`, not by disabling SELinux
nginx needs to run as root
steps.explain: Files created outside the standard web root get a default label that the web server's SELinux domain may not read.

steps.title: systemctl to OpenRC
prompt: Write `string ToOpenRc(string command)` translating a systemd command for Alpine:
- a leading `sudo` is kept; a `.service` suffix on the name is dropped
solution: string Svc(string s) => s.EndsWith(".service") ? s.Substring(0, s.Length - 8) : s;
hints: Split into words, peel off `sudo`, check `systemctl`.
Handle the special shapes (`list-units`, `enable --now`) before the simple 3-word ones.
template: Dojo.Eq("restart", "rc-service nginx restart", ToOpenRc("systemctl restart nginx"));
Dojo.Eq("status with sudo", "sudo rc-service sshd status", ToOpenRc("sudo systemctl status sshd"));
Dojo.Eq("enable", "rc-update add nginx default", ToOpenRc("systemctl enable nginx.service"));
Dojo.Eq("disable", "rc-update del crond default", ToOpenRc("systemctl disable crond"));
Dojo.Eq("enable --now", "sudo rc-update add redis default && sudo rc-service redis start", ToOpenRc("sudo systemctl enable --now redis"));
